true_answer: 30 0. Introduction and Preliminaries Notice that while 2 ∈ A , it is wrong to write 2 ∈ P( A ) since none of the elements in P( A ) are numbers! On the other hand, we do have { 2 }∈P( A ) because { 2 } ⊆ A . What does a subset of P( A ) look like? Notice that { 2 } ⊈ P( A ) because not everything in { 2 } is in P( A ) . But we do have {{ 2 }} ⊆ P( A ) . The only element of {{ 2 }} is the set { 2 } which is also an element of P( A ) . We could take the collection of all subsets of P( A ) and call that P(P( A )) . Or even the power set of that set of sets of sets.
